title: Architecture review - KV cache multi-route notes
content:
Date: 2026-03-24
Time: 10:00 - 11:15 PT
Location: Zoom / #eng-arch channel
Attendees: Ethan Kim (chair), Priya Rao, Lena Hoffman, Miguel Torres, Samir Desai, Rachel Ng (notes), Alex Chen (observability)
Purpose: Continue architecture review for KV cache sharding and multi-route routing strategy for low-latency inference. This meeting follows up on previous RFC and March design notes.

Summary
- Revisited proposals for sharding KV cache across GPU instances and routing decisions when multiple compatible model variants exist.
- Focus on correctness of KV lookup, cross-shard consistency, and graceful fallback when shards are temporarily unavailable.
- Evaluated trade-offs between per-model shards vs. shared-shard pools and per-customer isolation.

Key discussion points
1) Shard ownership model   - Option A (per-model/per-version shard): simplest for correctness and eviction isolation; increases memory overhead and reduces reuse across models.   - Option B (shared shard pool keyed by prefix hash): better utilization, lower memory overhead, more complex eviction and tenant isolation.   - Decision: move forward with hybrid approach: per-model primary shards, with an optional shared read-only pool for cold prefixes and cross-model reuse. Rationale: preserves isolation and predictable latency for hot models while enabling cache reuse for lower-priority workloads.

2) Routing and request handling   - Requests include model_id, model_version, route_policy (latency_priority|cost_priority), and optional allow_shared_pool flag.   - Router will prefer primary per-model shard if available; if primary is warm and below evict threshold route there. If primary is missing/prefers cost, consult shared pool candidates.   - Fallbacks: if shard lookup fails due to transient error, route to compatible model variant in same region with degraded QoS, with a circuit-breaker backoff.

3) Consistency guarantees and KV cache correctness   - Strong requirement: KV cache must never return stale KV entries for the same sequence position in a single inference request. We ensure this by binding KV entries to (model_version, prefix_hash, token_position) keys and by versioned shard manifests.   - Eviction races: use lightweight lease on writes and epoch numbers in shard manifests to prevent returning entries from an old shard after a shard move.

4) Eviction and memory management   - Primary shards use LRU with sticky entries for recent prefixes; shared pool uses segment-based sampling eviction.   - Autoscaling: when GPU memory pressure crosses 85% on a node, trigger background demotion of least-recently-used entries and signal router to avoid scheduling new primary shards to that node.

5) Observability and SLOs   - Instrument: per-shard hit/miss rates, tail-latency for KV lookup, cross-shard hop counts, and fallback rates.   - Dashboards: new per-route panels in Redwood Console (devs: Alex + Priya to prototype).   - Alerts: KV-miss spike and fallback-to-variant should trigger P3 if sustained >5m and P1 if impacting error-rate or tail latency.

Decisions made
- Adopt hybrid shard model: per-model primary + optional shared read-only pool.- Routing policy: prefer primary shard; use shared pool when allow_shared_pool is true or under load; use circuit-breaker and fallback to compatible variant on transient failures.- Add versioned shard manifests and lightweight leases to prevent stale reads.

Open questions / risks
- Security / data isolation: shared pool could leak cross-tenant data if not carefully keyed. Action: encryption-in-use for shared pool entries and stricter key namespaces. (Owner: Samir)
- Complexity of router: adding shared-pool logic increases routing complexity and testing surface. Need staging rollout. (Owner: Priya)
- Memory accounting across mixed workloads: need a simulation run to estimate hit-rate improvements vs memory costs. (Owner: Miguel)

Action items (owners and ETA)
- Samir: Draft shared-pool encryption/keying design and threat model. Due 2026-03-31.
- Priya: Implement router integration test harness with simulated shard outages and allow_shared_pool toggles. Due 2026-04-07.- Miguel: Run memory/hit-rate simulation for hybrid model using last 30 days of production traces (sampled). Report by 2026-04-02.- Alex + Rachel: Prototype dashboard panels for per-shard metrics and add alert definitions. Due 2026-04-06.

Next steps / rollout plan- Prototype hybrid shard in staging with a small set of canary models and traffic split (2% traffic) for 2 weeks. Verify latency, hit-rate, and fallback behavior.- If staging metrics meet SLOs, run a gradual rollout to low-priority hosted API customers, then to Dedicated pools behind canary policy.

Notes & references- Related RFCs and meeting notes: architecture-review-kv-cache-sharding-rfc-142.json, architecture-review-kv-cache-routing-notes-2026-02-26.json, architecture-review-kv-cache-sharding-meeting-notes-2026-03-03.json- Jira: JIRA-ARCH-884 tracks implementation epics and sub-tasks.

Parking lot (non-blocking items)- Consider per-tenant soft limits in the shared pool to prevent noisy neighbors.- Explore hardware-aware placement (NVLink adjacency) for shards with high cross-call locality.

Recorded by: Rachel Ng
Reviewer: Ethan Kim
